analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (base lines 798-1209 and 1210-1617). The PR changes only this documentation file. The visible patch has two hunks. The first, at base lines 404-407, rewrites the model-load eviction text to add `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad`. The second, at head lines 1050-1070, adds text on segmented paged KV admission: parked free 64 MiB segments (capped at min(2 GiB, slot grant/8) and kept outside the grant, floor and ledger charge) and zero-fill-on-demand host pages. The patch excerpt is truncated and the second hunk is incomplete, so the full change is not visible. The supplied base units do not contain the changed regions, so I examined them only as surrounding context.

Security-relevant observations:
- Parked segments are retained KV memory outside the ledger charge. If residual KV data in them is not zeroed, this touches T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory) and A-001. The excerpt says new segments use zero-fill-on-demand pages. It does not show whether reinstalled parked segments are scrubbed between requests or tenants. The docs say a released row's segments are reinstalled on the next admission of the same size class, but the patch text is cut off.
- Memory held outside the ledger could affect availability (T-029 and the memory-accounting contracts). The 2 GiB cap and the grant/8 bound limit this.
- This is a documentation-only change. I found no concrete security regression in the visible text, and the code behavior is unverified.

Next-pass questions:
- Does the parking path in provider-swift (referenced in the truncated patch) zero or overwrite parked KV contents before reuse?
- Does uncharged parked memory interact correctly with load-feasibility checks and eviction?
- Does `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad` drop the parked segments before the load gate?

The pooled-segment reuse scrubbing question is material to T-028, so I request deeper review once the code is available.
